pr_title: Fixes issue where failed start of OpenXR causes issues
pr_body:
We recently changed the way OpenXR manages extensions. This resulted in graphics API extension not being cleaned up if OpenXR was requested but failed to start. When using the Vulkan graphics API this results in the Vulkan hooks remaining in place causing a number of flow on issues.

We're now properly cleaning up the graphics API extension on failure and presenting a message to the user that while OpenXR was requested, it failed to start.

OpenXR will fail to start if:
- No OpenXR runtime is installed
- SteamVR is used but no headset is connected
- WMR is used natively as it only supports DirectX.

This likely fixes #71266 and fixes #64584

### System information

Windows 10 version 22H2, GeForce Game Ready Driver Version 528.02, GTX 1070

### Issue description

Since Beta 11 this error is given whenever a project is run in the forward+ renderer with OpenXR enabled. This error is not present with Beta 10 and previous versions.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38119387/212044209-1179b908-f010-47a1-ae53-bc2faadc30de.png)

I've tested with projects created in previous versions as well as the current version (Beta 11)

### Steps to reproduce

Create project, enable OpenXR in project settings, and run.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
It would be good to run this from console with `--verbose` to get some more info but we've been adding a lot of checks to make sure the hardware on computers can actually run the renderer. Some limitations were being ignored until Godot crashed when you tried ran into the places where they were used.

That said, we may have become too strict in places where most of the renderer works and we should simply be disabling a feature.

@BastiaanOlij  It looks like the initial call to ``vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices`` (the one to ascertain GPU count) is failing.

I wonder if this is a false positive from our error checking as ``vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices`` can return ``VK_INCOMPLETE`` on success. Although that is only supposed to happen when ``pPhysicalDevices`` is not ``NULL`` as far as I can tell.

From the [spec](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices.html)
> If pPhysicalDeviceCount is less than the number of physical devices available, at most pPhysicalDeviceCount structures will be written, and VK_INCOMPLETE will be returned instead of VK_SUCCESS, to indicate that not all the available physical devices were returned.
Also, this may be a duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/64584

That is really strange because this is the proper way of handling all enumerations in Vulkan (and most Khronos APIs) and this has been unchanged for some time now.

> This is what happens when errors are printed from multiple threads simultaneously. I'm not sure it indicates a memory issue

Have we started any threads this early on?

I doubt that is the problem also seeing this previously worked. Note that VK_INCOMPLETE is only returned when you call `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` with the 3rd parameter set, so the second time we call it when we're actually retrieving the device information.

See: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices.html
```
If pPhysicalDevices is NULL, then the number of physical devices available is returned in pPhysicalDeviceCount.
Otherwise, pPhysicalDeviceCount must point to a variable set by the user to the number of elements in the pPhysicalDevices array,
and on return the variable is overwritten with the number of handles actually written to pPhysicalDevices.

If pPhysicalDeviceCount is less than the number of physical devices available,
at most pPhysicalDeviceCount structures will be written,
and VK_INCOMPLETE will be returned instead of VK_SUCCESS,
to indicate that not all the available physical devices were returned.
```

Specifically that last bit, which doesn't apply to us because we will specify the correct number of devices as we just retrieved this information.

Seeing the weird errors around the `GalaxyOverlayVkLayer` layers, I wonder if incompatible layers were installed on this device. I don't believe we even instruct Vulkan to include those so this would have been configured externally.

Ok, wrote this on the other PR as well. I just ran into the same error and suddenly realized what is likely going on here.

When you enable OpenXR, Godot will attempt to start OpenXR. The problem here is that when you use a runtime like SteamVR, SteamVR will actually exit if no headset is found.

As under OpenXR, OpenXR is responsible for starting Vulkan, and OpenXR is now in an undefined state, things start to go wrong.

I'll improve the checking around OpenXR.
